sec: ADPKD vs ARPKD vs juvenile nephronophthisis table · p791

items.q: Match the age of presentation — 1) ADPKD  2) ARPKD  3) Juvenile nephronophthisis … A) Young adult > perinatal  B) Perinatal  C) 4–6 years
items.exp: Age of presentation: ADPKD — young adult > perinatal; ARPKD — perinatal; juvenile nephronophthisis — 4–6 years. (Book p791)

items.q: A 5-year-old child with renal failure has a small shrunken kidney on imaging with only a few cysts. Which disease does the table give as presenting at 4–6 years?
opts: Medullary sponge kidney, an acquired middle-aged disease
items.exp: Juvenile nephronophthisis presents at 4–6 years; ADPKD in young adults (perinatal in some) and ARPKD perinatally. (Book p791)

items.q: Match the kidney size and number of cysts — 1) ADPKD  2) ARPKD  3) Juvenile nephronophthisis … A) Enlarged kidneys with multiple cysts  B) Enlarged kidneys with multiple cysts  C) Enlarged kidneys with few cysts
items.exp: Table: ADPKD — enlarged kidneys with multiple cysts; ARPKD — enlarged kidneys with multiple cysts; juvenile nephronophthisis — (kidney size not enlarged) with few cysts. (Book p791)

items.q: Cyst infection is common (++) in ADPKD but not seen in ARPKD or juvenile nephronophthisis.
opts: False — cyst infection is commonest in ARPKD
False — cyst infection occurs in all three equally
items.exp: Cyst infection row: ADPKD ++; ARPKD –; juvenile nephronophthisis –. (Book p791)

items.q: Match the blood pressure finding — 1) ADPKD  2) ARPKD  3) Juvenile nephronophthisis … A) High  B) N/low due to tubular loss  C) High
items.exp: BP row: ADPKD — high; ARPKD — high; juvenile nephronophthisis — normal/low due to tubular loss. (Book p791)

items.q: A child with juvenile nephronophthisis has a blood pressure of 90/60 mmHg. Why is BP not high, unlike in ADPKD/ARPKD?
opts: Normal or low BP is due to tubular loss (salt wasting)
Because the disease is glomerular and spares tubules
Because the kidney is enlarged with multiple cysts
items.exp: BP in juvenile nephronophthisis is N/low due to tubular loss, reflecting the salt-wasting tubulopathy, in contrast to the high BP of ADPKD and ARPKD. (Book p791)

items.q: Match the nephrocalcinosis finding — 1) ADPKD  2) ARPKD  3) Juvenile nephronophthisis … A) ++  B) 25%  C) No nephrocalcinosis
items.exp: Nephrocalcinosis row: ADPKD ++; ARPKD 25%; juvenile nephronophthisis no nephrocalcinosis. (Book p791)

items.q: In the comparison table, nephrocalcinosis occurs in ARPKD in what proportion?
items.exp: ARPKD shows nephrocalcinosis in 25% of cases; ADPKD ++ and juvenile nephronophthisis none. (Book p791)

items.q: Match the CNS manifestation — 1) ADPKD  2) ARPKD  3) Juvenile nephronophthisis … A) Joubert's (cerebellar aplasia)  B) None  C) Aneurysm
items.exp: CNS manifestations: ADPKD — aneurysm; ARPKD — none; juvenile nephronophthisis — Joubert's (cerebellar aplasia). (Book p791)

items.q: Match the liver manifestation — 1) ADPKD  2) ARPKD  3) Juvenile nephronophthisis … A) Cyst  B) Portal hypertension  C) None
items.exp: Liver manifestations: ADPKD — cyst; ARPKD — portal hypertension (congenital hepatic fibrosis/Caroli); juvenile nephronophthisis — none. (Book p791)

items.q: Match the chromosome involved — 1) ADPKD  2) ARPKD  3) Juvenile nephronophthisis … A) 16/4  B) 6  C) 2
items.exp: Chromosome row: ADPKD 16/4 (PKD1 16p, PKD2 4q); ARPKD 6 (PKHD1); juvenile nephronophthisis 2 (NPHP1). (Book p791)
